sections.heading: About the wool
sections.html: Everything here is felted wool, which means a sweater that shrank on purpose. Good wool is wool that has been washed hot and dried hot, cut from coats and skirts from the thrift store, and catalogued in the wool library by weight. If it pills and survives, it quilts.

sections.title: Join the circle
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Twenty dollars a year, a pattern library, tea, and eleven people who will teach you the whipstitch until it looks right.

sections.heading: What dues cover
sections.html: Meetings, the wool library, dye days, and the pattern drawer. Beginners are paired with a stitch partner for the first season, and the first kit is on the circle. Open the membership form and choose a level.

items.q: I have never stitched. Is that all right?
items.a: The circle was founded by two women who had never stitched either. The beginner kit and a patient partner are standing inventory.

items.q: Do I need a sewing machine?
items.a: No. This is all hand work, done with one needle, one thread, and better conversation than any machine allows.

items.q: What does the wool cost me?
items.a: A trip to the thrift store. Sweaters cost less there than felt by the yard, and the shrinking is part of the fun.

sections.title: About the circle
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Founded around a church basement table in 2009 with one pattern and two borrowed scissors.

sections.heading: How the circle grew
sections.html:
The first winter there were four of us and one pattern, traced by hand onto paper bags because nobody owned a copier. The second winter there were nine, and the dye days started because wool in one color is a hobby but wool in nine colors is a guild.

We keep the old habits: patterns traced and shared freely, felted wool traded instead of bought, and every finished piece shown before it is given away. Most of them are given away, which is the point of a penny rug anyway.

items.quote: I joined to get out of the house one night a week. I stayed because someone finally taught me a stitch my mother never got to.
items.author: E., member since 2014

items.quote: The wool library is the only library where I have returned something better than I borrowed it.
items.author: C., dye day regular
